scope: Proposition 10.2 (Full-time localization) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 156. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the setting of Equations (10.2) and (10.3), a permitted further selection admits full-time charts C with tangential width one and normal width gC = g2N2u 0 . (10.7) Their labels are known by the original p1 with actual subpower lists. The native test remains P∗. If nC and yC(t) are the normal and affine center of C, then every retained Q1-incidence satisfies, after a consistent choice of signs, |n1 − nC| ≤ K0g1, |nC · (y′ 1 − y′ C)| ≤ K0g1. (10.8) All assignments, geometric tests and coordinate changes have tempered bounds within each fixed Ei.
